answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on probability mass reachable from trusted roots, not the number of identities claimed. A sybil cluster with a sparse external cut has low conductance: few walk transitions can enter it from the honest region. With capped walk exposure and root-normalized voting, this limits the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. The signal crosses the lagoon through verified edges, not by scaling a summit of self-created accounts.
